records.region: Atacama, Chile; unnamed mountain feeder–Valeriano–Conay–Tránsito–Huasco, Santa Juana reservoir and Pacific estuary.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative identity of the connected selected river system, anchored in its downstream receiving river; not a uniform name for the mountain feeder, Valeriano, Conay, Tránsito or reservoir passage.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Original official hydrographic and wetland cartography accounts for the entire selected mountain-feeder–Valeriano–Conay–Tránsito–Huasco corridor, the Santa Juana reservoir connection, and the coastal estuary/Pacific terminal. Río Huasco is supported as representative system identity. The initial feeder remains unnamed in this finding, and distinct upstream names and waterbody settings are preserved.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the connected selected river system, anchored in its downstream receiving river; not a uniform name for the mountain feeder, Valeriano, Conay, Tránsito or reservoir passage.

component_scope_limits: Río Huasco names the receiving river downstream of the Tránsito–Carmen junction and serves only as the representative system candidate for the full selected object.
The southern initial feeder has no established component hydronym here. Its mapped channel/wetland continuity is supported independently of its name.
Valeriano, Conay and Tránsito retain their component scopes. Santa Juana is a reservoir name, not a substitute river name.
The wetland inventory's broad Rio Huasco labels appear on geographically distinct upstream fluvial polygons; they are not evidence of uniform scalar naming.
Laguna Grande, Laguna Chica, Laguna Valeriano and Laguna del Encierro are not assigned as selected lake passages merely because they belong to the neighboring drainage. Unknown names remain null.

records.supported_name_scope: The repeated Rio Cassiporé labels on the inspected primary maps establish the representative main river through the northeastern interior corridor, Vila Velha, the northward Cabo Orange lowlands and the estuary by Taperebá. The southwestern opening feeder is left unnamed, and the selected western tributary has its own Rio Segundo Braço correspondence.
records.completion_scope: All five selected FIDs were read against primary original cartography at ordinary generalized corridor/component scale. The first headward portion is poorly resolved in the municipal map alone but is depicted in the more detailed CPRM sheet; no actual headward, tributary or terminal source-coverage gap remains. No geometry modification, pointwise revalidation, precise spring location or current shoreline assertion is made.
records.region: Amapá, Brazil; Cassiporé mainstem, selected lower Rio Segundo Braço tributary and Taperebá estuary.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative downstream river-system identity; not a uniform name for the selected southwestern feeder or the separately selected lower Rio Segundo Braço tributary.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The Rio Regina headwater branch is mapped separately from the selected southwestern feeder. Rio Segundo Braço is the selected tributary, not a second uniformly named Cassiporé mainstem. Rio Anotaié and Rio Arapari lie west of the selected interior corridor; the Cunani is a separate drainage to the southeast. Lago Maruani is a lateral lower-river connection, not a selected through-lake passage. The separate Uaçá/Oiapoque drainage is not the terminal receiving river.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
